title: Silver Cascade Lending — onramp call capture
content:
Context:
- Customer: Silver Cascade Lending (mid-market consumer loan platform). Evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for underwriting-assistant and triage assistant. High sensitivity on PII, regulatory audit trail, and predictable latency for real-time chat inside loan officer UI.
- Call attendees: Maya K (Redwood CSM), Diego M (Redwood solutions eng), Priya A (acct exec), Thomas Lee (Silver Cascade eng lead), Anya Patel (risk/product), Rajesh Iyer (security).

High-level asks from Silver Cascade:
1) PII-safe private deployment (need HSM / KMS integration and audit logs retained 1y).
2) Latency target: 95th perc < 250ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens); baseline traffic initially ~50 rps during office hours, bursting to 120 rps for 5–10m windows.
3) Deterministic fallbacks: if primary model overloaded, fall back to smaller quantized model without changing output schema.
4) Explicit prompt/response retention controls and a deletion workflow for user-initiated data removal.
5) Version pinning for models and ability to audit prompt sets used in regressions (qa + compliance).

Technical notes from Thomas (customer):
- Prefers on-premise gateway inside their VPC; they run on GCP (us-central1) and have strict egress policies (no external network to unknown IPs).
- They want TLS mutual auth and allowlist of Redwood control-plane IPs for startup only.
- Existing infra uses HashiCorp Vault for secrets; would prefer Redwood to support native Vault integration or at least use customer-managed KMS key for model keys.
- Typical inference payload: ~80 tokens prompt + few-shot examples (1–3 examples), expecting 20–30 token answer. Many short synchronous chat calls from loan-officer UI.

Gotchas / risk areas (call observations):
- Egress rules + private control plane: they will not accept outgoing websockets to unknown hosts. Need to document the minimal control-plane endpoints and exact ports (ask infra).
- Audit log storage: they asked for 1-year retention and indexed fields (user_id, operation, model_version). We'll need to show example log schema for compliance review.
- Burst handling: they want guaranteed latency under bursts; explain Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private sizing. Suggest initial Dedicated pool sizing guidance (see action items).
- PII scrubbing: they want optional in-flight redaction (PII filter) before logging — check if Redwood can plug a pre-request filter that strips/obfuscates SSNs and card numbers.
- Cost sensitivity: They asked for rough TCO for Dedicated vs Private; finance will need per-token estimate plus infra overhead.

Initial suggested architecture (sketch):
- Private control plane running in customer VPC with restricted egress to Redwood update endpoints.
- Inference dataplane: managed nodes in their VPC (BYO GPU or Redwood-managed within VPC) depending on procurement. Start with small Dedicated-like pool inside VPC (N1), autoscale policy limited to 2x nominal.
- KMS: integrate with Vault/HSM. Provide instructions for creating key and granting Redwood service principal (or pull model: bring-your-key + client-side decrypt).
- Logs: forward to customer Splunk/Cloud Logging with Redwood-provided structured events. Provide mapping for required fields.

Operational parameters to validate:
- Recommended model family: Mistral-7B-Q8 as fallback, primary: Mistral-16B or similar (matches their quality request). Provide performance matrix with 95/99 latencies for token-length buckets.
- Batching policy: set max batch latency 10ms and concurrency cap per worker to preserve tail latency.
- KV cache TTL: default 30s for session-level caching; can be tuned.

Action items (owner — ETA):
- Diego: Produce minimal control-plane whitelist + ports doc (RC-PR-001). Due: 2024-09-28.
- Maya: Send example audit-log schema + sample JSON lines for one week of traffic (anonymized). Due: 2024-10-02.
- Diego & Thomas: Quick feasibility call on Vault integration (20m). Schedule: week of 2024-09-30.
- Solutions eng (Diego): Draft sizing recommendation (GPU types, pool size) for 50–120 rps with latency target. Include Dedicated vs Private cost roughs. Due: 2024-10-06.
- Priya: Prepare commercial note (expected spend bands) and attach to proposal. Due: 2024-10-04.

Prompts / sample usage (captured during demo):
- Prompt pattern 1 (triage): 'User message + account metadata + 1 example' => expects structured JSON: {resolution: 'answer|need-human', suggested_next_steps: [], confidence: 0.0} (they require high-quality structured output).
- Prompt pattern 2 (underwriting assist): long context (customer profile + credit history) + targeted question. Need to ensure tokenization is tracked for cost forecasting.

Open questions / follow-ups (need answers from infra/product):
- Can Redwood support mutual TLS client certs for the control-plane connection? (Diego to confirm with infra).
- Exact log retention and encryption-at-rest guarantee for forwarded logs to customer-managed storage.
- Is there an off-the-shelf PII redaction plugin (pre-request) we can propose? If not, list recommended approach (rule-based regex + model-based scrub).
- Model pinning UI: show Thomas a quick flow for pinning and rollback in Console. (Product to demo).

Notes-to-self (quick):
- Emphasize audit trail and reproducible prompts for compliance in next deck.
- Keep cost bands conservative (assume busy-hour QPS sustained for 30m windows).
- When sharing PRICING: include overhead for private-control-plane (network, logs, ops) + monthly reserved commit for Dedicated pool.

Meeting follow-up plan:
1) Send this capture with action owners + rough timeline (today).
2) Attach recommended sizing matrix + sample audit log in next email.
3) Book vault-integration 20m with Thomas + Diego.

Quick contact list:
- Thomas Lee (Silver Cascade): thomas.lee@silvercascade.com (engineering lead)
- Anya Patel (product/risk): anya.patel@silvercascade.com
- Rajesh Iyer (security): rajesh.iyer@silvercascade.com

End-of-note.

'Notes' style: messy but actionable — leave in Drive as working copy until we finalize proposer doc.
